The core threat is “imported inflation.” Unlike demand-driven price rises, this phenomenon occurs when external factors—soaring energy costs, disrupted shipping routes, and skyrocketing insurance premiums—push up prices regardless of domestic monetary policy. With the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for nearly 20% of global oil supply, potentially becoming a conflict zone, analysts forecast crude oil prices could exceed $150–$200 per barrel.
